data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root ‘asl,’ meaning ‘sweet, delightful.’ In Islamic culture, Asal is a name with spiritual significance, symbolizing the sweetness of faith and the delight of worshiping Allah. The name Asal carries the meaning “Sweet, Delightful” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asal usually hope their child will grow to embody sweet, delightful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the sweetness of faith and devotion in Islam.
data.etymology: Asal belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sweet, Delightful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asal total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: The name Asal carries a positive connotation in Islamic society, as it implies that the person carries the sweetness of faith within them. It may also be used metaphorically to indicate someone who brings joy, happiness or pleasure to others around them.
data.spiritual_significance: In the spiritual context, the name Asal underscores the importance of savoring the sweetness of faith, and of striving to keep our hearts connected to Allah. It serves as a reminder to constantly seek nachas (spiritual satisfaction) from Allah and to value the sweetness of our faith over worldly pleasures or momentary delights. The name Asal also carries a deeper reminder, echoing Rumi's famous quote "The suckling of the roses is the desire to attain the Beloved," - encouraging us to look beyond the physical world and to focus our desire and thirst towards a sacred, spiritual connection with Allah.
